clue.text: Pavarotti's OK in an opera house

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: Manon is an opera by Massenet (and Puccini wrote Manon Lescaut)
Pavarotti was Italian, and the Italian for yes, okay, is si

explanation.surface: The great tenor gives his approval to an opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opera house' reads as one phrase, but 'house' alone is the definition and 'an opera' is MANON.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a large and grand residence, a kind of house.

clue.text: Position in which half of Russian jets take off

indicators.note: only half the word for Russian jets, its front two letters, is used

parts.note: MiGs are Russian fighter jets
to doff a hat is to take it off

explanation.surface: A spot where half of a squadron of Russian jets get airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Position' is a cricket field position: mid-off stands near the bowler on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-off is a fielding place in cricket, a position on the field.

clue.text: Stretchy hose only sprayed neighbours' borders

indicators.note: sprayed scatters these letters into a new order
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A garden hose was turned only on the edges of the neighbours' plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' looks like a garden hosepipe but means stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are stockings, hosiery, made of stretchy nylon fibre.

clue.text: Fake barrier doesn't open

indicators.note: the word for barrier loses its opening letter

parts.note: a limitation is a barrier or restriction

explanation.surface: A gate that won't open is only a sham.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a copy, something not genuine.

clue.text: _ora B_? Completing it would be smart

parts.note: the gaps are filled to make Nora Batty, a character in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine; the missing first letter and final four letters are the answer

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blanks puzzle promising that solving it would be clever.
explanation.walkthrough: Nora Batty, from the long-running British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine, was famous for wrinkled stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and smartly dressed.

clue.text: A bit of help: one across is a house

indicators.note: a small bit of the word help is taken here, namely its opening letter

parts.note: an means one, as in 'an apple'
over can mean across, as in 'over the road'

explanation.surface: A tip from a puzzle-solver: the first across answer is a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one across' looks like a cross-reference to 1 Across, itself a house, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover is the royal house that ruled Britain from George I to Victoria.

clue.text: When kids knock, greeting tiny one in the middle

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, like hello
wee is Scottish for tiny

indicators.note: only the central letter of the word one is taken

explanation.surface: Children knock and greet the smallest one among them.
explanation.definitionFit: On 31 October children go door to door trick-or-treating, knocking for sweets.

clue.text: Coming soon, time when the earth cools

parts.note: nigh means near, approaching soon

explanation.surface: A warning that the planet will soon cool down.
explanation.definitionFit: After sunset the ground loses heat, so the dark hours are the cool part of the day.

clue.text: Burning dinner, daughter cuts very hot potato

indicators.note: cuts means the daughter's letter goes into the other pieces

parts.note: in can mean hot, fashionable
aloo is the Hindi word for potato, familiar from Indian menus

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: dinner is burning while a daughter chops a scalding potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning' means spicy hot, not on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiery Indian curry, a meal that burns the mouth.

clue.text: Face covered in spots, son not caring

indicators.note: the face, or front letter, of the word for spots is hidden, so it is removed

parts.note: freckles are small brown spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A spotty teenage son who doesn't care about his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless describes someone heedless of danger or consequences.

clue.text: City sandwich shop that's hot inside

indicators.note: says the letter for hot is placed within the shop's name

parts.note: a deli sells sandwiches and cooked meats
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A city sandwich bar that is warm indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is a major city in northern India, home to the capital New Delhi.

clue.text: Alien on film set, flipping good on camera

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole string of pieces over, so it is read backwards
in an across clue, on places the alien after the film and set pieces

parts.note: cine is a prefix and word for film, as in cine camera
to gel is to set, as jelly does
ET is the alien of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: An alien appears on a film set and turns out to be good on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but reverses everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone telegenic looks attractive and comes across well on television.

clue.text: Layoffs at lab not fixed, pretend management

indicators.note: letters that are fixed are repaired or rearranged into proper order

explanation.surface: Redundancies at a laboratory remain unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fixed' looks like one phrase; 'not' is part of the fodder and 'fixed' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In this game fans pick imaginary teams of real players and score points, playing at being a club manager.

clue.text: Tiny couple twists at the end of dance

indicators.text: couple twists at the end of
indicators.note: a couple, two letters, at the end of the word get turned round

parts.note: the minuet is a stately dance in triple time

explanation.surface: A small pair of dancers spins as the dance finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple twists at the end of' swaps the last two letters ET of MINUET to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute (my-NEWT) means extremely small, a synonym of tiny.

clue.text: New locum changed drug, accepted reluctantly

indicators.note: changed tells us these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A new stand-in doctor switched a patient's medicine, which was received grudgingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is not wanted, so it is received with reluctance.

clue.text: Go over teacher's negative feedback

definitions.meaning: to travel from one side to the other, as over a road
the mark a teacher puts beside a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A teacher revises work and gives critical comments.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross is to go over, and an X mark beside an answer shows it was wrong.

clue.text: Decontamination caught scrawny rat

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
lean means thin, scrawny
to rat on someone is to inform, to sing to the police

explanation.surface: Pest control has trapped a thin rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' is a verb, to betray, which matches the slang 'sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansing is making something clean, freeing it from contamination.

clue.text: Risk rows again holding up fuel production line

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the words Risk rows again hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Another round of arguments threatens to stall fuel production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' marks a run hidden across 'Risk rows again'; 'up' reverses it, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasworks is a plant that manufactures fuel gas, such as town gas from coal.

clue.text: Cycling loses its attraction, maybe hailstones pepper ground

indicators.note: cycling moves the front letter round to the back of the word for losing attraction

parts.note: something that palls becomes dull and loses its appeal
hailstones are an example of ice

explanation.surface: A cyclist loses interest as hailstones batter the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves the P of PALLS to the end, giving ALLSP.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice, also called Jamaica pepper, is a dried berry usually sold ground.

clue.text: Spent nothing out, presumably

definitions.meaning: read literally: if nothing is out, everything is inside

explanation.surface: Someone paid nothing, they suppose.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is informal for exhausted; read as words, it also says everything is inside.

clue.text: Watch part of victory turning bloody

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: turning means the word for bloody is read backwards

parts.note: something bloody is red

explanation.surface: A violent turn in the course of a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The winder is the crown on a mechanical watch turned to wind the spring.

clue.text: Lodging suit finally after libel spread

indicators.note: the last letter of suit comes after the rearranged letters
spread scatters the letters of libel into a new order
finally takes the closing letter of suit

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is finally brought after defamation circulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like a lawsuit with 'libel'; it only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is a place where soldiers are lodged, often in a private house.

clue.text: Antique silver Eros lady displayed in odd locations

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: only the letters in the odd positions, first, third and so on, are shown

explanation.surface: An old silver statue of Eros and a lady shown in strange places.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old means very old, having existed for ages, like an antique.

clue.text: With one weak card, holding busted flush; going 17 on that?

indicators.note: holding means the other pieces enclose the shuffled letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
thin can mean weak, as in a thin excuse
the king is a playing card

indicators.note: busted means broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poker player with a feeble hand and a failed flush wonders whether to bet everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 Across is ALL IN: pushing all your chips in on a weak hand is hoping against reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting everything on a busted flush is believing what you hope rather than what is likely.

clue.text: Newspaper covers one aspect

indicators.note: the newspaper's letters go round the outside of the word for one

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports on one side of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one side or feature of something, an aspect of it.

clue.text: Region of Pluto in darkness with sun going down

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for sun moves lower, to the bottom

parts.note: shade is partial darkness

explanation.surface: A dark patch on the planet Pluto as the sun sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluto' suggests the dwarf planet but is the Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was the Roman god ruling the underworld, the realm the Greeks called by this name.

clue.text: Water for shower artist stored remotely?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
data kept on remote servers is said to be in the cloud

explanation.surface: A painter keeps something for the shower off-site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stored remotely' reads IN CLOUD, the computing phrase for data kept on distant servers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain cloud holds the water that falls as a shower of rain.

clue.text: Bishop abandons tall ladies in low dome

indicators.note: the bishop's letter is left behind, taken out of the rest

parts.note: big can mean tall, as in a big man
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the ladies is a women's toilet, a loo in British slang

explanation.surface: A bishop walks away from tall women under a low cupola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' here is the British word for a women's toilet, LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit snow house shaped like a low dome.

clue.text: Cover point, he catches Cook

indicators.note: catches means the outer pieces hold the cooking word between them

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
to heat food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at cover point takes a catch off Cook, the England batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover point' is a cricket fielding position and Alastair Cook an England batsman; 'Cover' is the definition and 'point' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a blade is to put it in its scabbard, covering it.

clue.text: Seeing father on telly, moan in front of him

indicators.note: the moan comes before the father, him referring back to him

parts.note: a sigh is a low moan
Father Ted is a British TV sitcom about an Irish priest

explanation.surface: A viewer spots a priest on television and groans at him.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted was a 1990s British sitcom about a priest on an Irish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighted means able to see, not blind.
